title: Prompt Engineering
summary: Prompt Engineering is the deliberate design, testing, and maintenance of the instructions that steer a generative AI model or agent. It defines the task, priorities, constraints, role boundaries, output contract, and acceptance criteria.
definition: Prompt Engineering is the deliberate design, testing, and maintenance of the instructions that steer a generative AI model or agent. It defines the task, priorities, constraints, role boundaries, output contract, and acceptance criteria. In production, it also includes persistent system or developer instructions and their priority relative to user requests and untrusted tool content. It engineers the instruction layer; context, tools, loops, and multi-agent orchestration remain separate design problems.

Instruction hierarchy is also security-relevant because agents must prioritize trusted system and developer instructions over conflicting user or tool content.
audiences.knowledgeWorkers: Strong prompts specify the objective, constraints, authoritative sources, expected output, and what must be checked before acceptance. The skill is increasingly to write a clear assignment and definition of done, not memorize prompt tricks.

example: A procurement team maintains a version-controlled vendor-analysis instruction defining the scoring framework, required evidence, prohibited assumptions, output schema, and escalation rules. Representative proposals are used to evaluate each revision before release.

misconception: Prompt Engineering is neither magic wording nor obsolete. Its modern role is disciplined instruction design: make the contract clear, keep it lean, and test it; use Context, Loop, and Graph Engineering for the surrounding system.
monitor: Instruction-following reliability; prompt-injection resistance; hierarchy conflicts; performance and cost by prompt version; structured-output reliability; and eval-driven prompt changes. Evidence: [1], [2], [3], [4], [5].
